scope: Review that one common runtime serves desktop and mobile and that Android exposes and qualifies every Vulkan-advertised Gallery scene and action.

common_owners.controller_semantics: GallerySession, GalleryRuntime and MobileGallerySession semantic commands

desktop: debug overlays, capture, calibration and scripted diagnostic loops
android: Activity, SurfaceView and Android lifecycle callbacks
touch and accessibility widget translation into semantic commands
display callback scheduling and atomic report storage
ios: display callback scheduling and atomic report storage

documented_exceptions: Desktop headless, capture and calibration paths use explicit GallerySession diagnostics because they are noninteractive tools.
Platform shells schedule display callbacks because Android, UIKit and desktop window systems supply different event loops; fixed-step admission and catch-up policy remain inside GallerySession.

android_device_evidence.application_lifecycle: background, foreground, surface recreation, resize, rotation and native teardown passed

verification.result: F7-01 through F7-23 are done and F7-99 owns the gallery-exit-review lock.

verification.check: Platform shell source audit plus parallel-mater-slang-architecture
verification.result: Common catalog, lifecycle, controller, frame policy, qualification and renderer ownership pass; only documented OS event, surface and presentation work remains in shells.
11/11 tracked physical-device artifacts match their recorded hashes.

verification.check: F7-18 qualification and performance report review
verification.result: 28/28 advertised scenes, 6/6 lifecycle checks and 6/6 control checks passed; two ordinary direct-presentation windows completed for every scene without thermal throttling.
PASS: Slang architecture audit, 14/14 Gallery Python tests and 28/28 roadmap workflow tests.

residual_risks: The Pixel 7 workload profile is not performance-qualified: second-window scene rates span 1.66 to 18.02 FPS, median 5.155 FPS, and 0 of 28 scenes reach 30 FPS.
The 640 by 288 phone render is visibly coarse; higher resolution should wait for measured physics improvements.
The frozen Info capture reports zero host frames per second; performance.json is the authoritative ordinary-frame measurement.
Physical Android runtime evidence currently covers one Pixel 7 and Mali-G710 driver combination.
The bounded 797-second sweep found no throttling; it is not a battery-endurance qualification.
